title: Reading academic papers
examples: How do I know what the main argument is before reading the whole paper?
What is the difference between the results and the discussion section?
Should I focus on the abstract or the conclusion first?

explain.say: First, you should read the abstract to get the main idea.

items: Covers the aim, methods, and key findings.
Helps you decide if the paper is relevant.

draw.text: Abstract: Summary of the whole paper

explain.say: Next, look closely at the figures and tables for data.
Then, read the discussion section to understand the meaning.
The abstract summarizes the whole paper quickly for you.
In a real report, the abstract gives you the core message right away.
A common mistake is thinking the results are the same as the discussion.

faq.q: What is the main purpose of the abstract?
faq.a: The abstract gives you a very short summary of the entire research paper. It helps you quickly decide if the paper is useful for your work.
asks: How do I summarize the paper quickly?

faq.q: Do I need to read the figures when I read a paper?
faq.a: Yes, figures and tables show the actual data the authors collected. They provide the visual evidence for the claims made in the text.

faq.q: What is the difference between results and discussion?
faq.a: The results section just reports what the data shows, without explaining it. The discussion section explains what those results actually mean.
asks: Should I confuse findings with meaning?

faq.q: Should I read the conclusion or the abstract first?
faq.a: Reading the abstract first is usually best because it gives you a balanced summary of the entire study's journey. The conclusion is often a restatement of the abstract.
asks: Which section is the most important?
Is the conclusion different from the abstract?

faq.q: What should I look for in the figures?
faq.a: You should look at the captions and the axes labels on the graphs. These tell you exactly what the numbers represent.
asks: How do I read a graph correctly?

facts: The abstract is a concise summary of the entire study.
Figures present data visually, such as graphs and charts.
The discussion section interprets the meaning of the findings.
You should read the abstract first for an overview.

quiz.why: The discussion is where authors explain the significance and meaning of the data shown.

wrong.0: The caption only explains what the graph shows, not why.
wrong.1: The results section only reports the numbers, it does not explain the meaning.
wrong.3: The abstract only gives a very short summary, not deep interpretation.

quiz.say: When reading a paper, what is the best order to gain a general understanding?
quiz.why: This order moves from a quick summary to visual evidence, and finally to deep interpretation.

wrong.1: Starting with figures can be overwhelming without context.
wrong.2: Starting with the discussion assumes you already know the results.
wrong.3: It is best to see the data (figures) before reading the interpretation (discussion).
